children: By Aamir Khalid
Australian shares ended higher on Thursday after paring sharp early gains, as easing bond yields and lower oil prices helped investors look past the U.S. Federal Reserve's first rate hike since 2023.
The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index
ended 0.4% higher at 8,732.40 points, after reaching as much as 1% earlier in the day. The benchmark ended up 0.3% on Wednesday.
Investors largely brushed aside the Fed's hawkish move, instead welcoming a pullback in U.S. Treasury yields from recent highs, supporting appetite for equities.

Attention now turns to the Reserve Bank of Australia's policy meeting later this month, with the Fed's hawkish shift reinforcing expectations that Australian interest rates could remain higher for longer.
"Investors had already accepted the Fed needed to raise rates in order to manage inflation in the region" said Grady Wulff, senior market analyst with Bell Direct.
"The rising bond yields has been a more recent story investors have had to grapple with hence the volatility in equities as a result of this new factor of consideration."
Banks
, gained 1.4%, its best day in over a month, with the "Big Four" gaining above 1% each.
"Banks are likely feeling some relief buying following several weak sessions in addition to higher rate expectations at home," added Wulff.
Brokerage Citi also upgraded its earnings forecasts for major banks, expecting higher business credit growth and stronger net interest margins due to higher rates.
Capping gains, miners
slipped 0.5%, with Rio Tinto
falling 0.1%
Energy stocks
fell as much as 2.2%, their worst session in three weeks, hurt by weakening oil prices.
Technology stocks
tumbled 1% while health
gained 1%.
The New Zealand benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index
rose 1% to 13,756.59 points. The island nation reported that economy slowed in the second quarter as the Middle East crisis weighed on growth.
